name: Yurutí
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 6 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Valencia Pérez, Elizabeth. 2014. Marcación de objeto diferencial (MOD) en la lengua yurutí. Trabajo de grado (Maestría en Lingüística), Universidad del Valle, Cali. 120 pp. Open access, handle 10893/9154. Cross-checked against Barnes, Janet. 1999. Tucano. In Dixon & Aikhenvald (eds.), The Amazonian Languages, 207-226. CUP (sec. 2.4 'Accent', p.212) and Ardila, Olga. 1998. Aspectos fonológicos de las lenguas tucano-orientales. Forma y Función 11: 41-54 (sec. 1.1 'El sistema tonal', p.45-46).
catalog_locator: sec. 7.1 'Fonética y Fonología', p.31; sec. 7.3 'Resumen', pp.39-40; sec. 8.1.2 'El Verbo', p.48.
catalog_quote: Con respecto a la prosodia, la lengua yurutí presenta ejemplos aislados de patrones tonales(-acentuales?) que marcan diferencias de significado, p.ej. en la palabra para guacamaya [mã:˥] y la palabra para camino [mã:˧]. No he realizado aún un estudio de este fenómeno fonológico en la lengua yurutí por no encontrar más de dos ejemplos que lo ilustren y porque no predice cambios al análisis de la estrategia MOD. (p.31) ... A nivel segmental y suprasegmental se identifican fenómenos como la aspiración, la glotalización y los patrones acentuales, que han sido motivo de estudio en otras lenguas TO (ver Stenzel, 2004; Chacón, 2010), pero que no se han caracterizado para el presente trabajo. (sec. 7.3) ... En yurutí las raíces verbales se componen de una a tres sílabas y no poseen un acento fijo, sino que éste varía bajo influencia de los morfemas que se le sufijan. (p.48)
world_status: statement found in an open source

(p.48)
new_statements.translation: As regards prosody, Yurutí shows isolated examples of tonal(-accentual?) patterns that distinguish meaning, e.g. the word for 'macaw' [mã: high] vs the word for 'path' [mã: mid]. I have not yet studied this phonological phenomenon in Yurutí, having found no more than two examples of it [...] (p.31) — In Yurutí, verb roots consist of one to three syllables and do not have a fixed accent; rather, it varies under the influence of the morphemes suffixed to them. (p.48)
new_statements.citation: Valencia Pérez, Elizabeth. 2014. Marcación de objeto diferencial (MOD) en la lengua yurutí. Trabajo de grado (Maestría en Lingüística), Universidad del Valle, Cali.
new_statements.locator: sec. 7.1 'Fonética y Fonología', printed p.31 (p.38); sec. 8.1.2 'El Verbo', printed p.48 (p.55)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File opened. Both quoted passages are present verbatim at the stated locators: (1) sec. 7.1, printed p.31 = p.38, the text: 'Con respecto a la prosodia, la lengua yurutí presenta ejemplos aislados de patrones tonales(-acentuales?) que marcan diferencias de significado, p.ej. en la palabra para guacamaya [mã:˥] y la palabra para camino [mã:˧]. No he realizado aún un estudio de este fenómeno fonológico en la lengua yurutí por no encontrar más de dos ejemplos que lo ilustren y porque no predice cambios al análisis de la estrategia MOD.' (the compilers '[..]' elides only the final clause); (2) sec. 8.1.2 'El Verbo', printed p.48 = p.55, the text: 'En yurutí las raíces verbales se componen de un…
new_statements.rule_in_words: No positional rule is given: the author reports that word accent in Yurutí is not fixed (at least on verb roots) and shifts depending on the suffixes attached, alongside isolated lexical pitch (tone) contrasts; she flags prosody as unanalysed. Barnes 1999 (family survey, p.212) adds that Yurutí is a pitch accent language with high vs low pitch and exactly one accented (high-pitched) syllable per phonological word, again without a placement rule.
new_statements.exceptions: None; statement restricted to verb roots and explicitly preliminary. Allophony notes (p.36-37) mention glide formation of /i/, /o/ 'donde hay una relajación en el patrón de acentuación', i.e. in unaccented position.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level (verb root + suffixes); Barnes 1999 frames the culminative accent over the phonological word. Valencia Pérez's phonetic transcriptions mark one stress per word with ['] (e.g. ['patu] 'coca', [do'ku-dʒa-ʋi] 'is pounding', [ba'hi] 'younger brother', [ke'ti] 'story') but give no rule.
new_statements.identity_note: Valencia Pérez 2014 describes the Yurutí (self-designation Wajiara) of Consuelo del Paca, upper Paca river, Vaupés, Colombia = Glottolog yuru1263 / ISO yui; same community as Benavidez & Díaz 2015 and Arango Giraldo 2017. Barnes 1999 and Ardila 1998 are family surveys citing Yurutí second-hand (Kinch & Kinch ms.). Ardila notes Yurutí is very close to Pisamira (a separate Glottolog languoid), which she describes as accentual rather than tonal — do not transfer Pisamira statements to Yurutí.

sources.locator: sec. 7.1 'Fonética y Fonología', printed p.31 (p.38); sec. 8.1.2 'El Verbo', printed p.48 (p.55)
sources.note: Ch. 7 'Fonología' is segmental + nasal harmony only. Sec. 7.1 p.31: isolated 'tonal(-accentual?)' pitch contrasts (guacamaya [mã:˥] vs camino [mã:˧]), prosody explicitly not studied; sec. 7.3 p.39-40: 'patrones acentuales' identified but not characterised; sec. 8.1.2 p.48: verb roots (1-3 syllables) have no fixed accent, accent shifts under suffixation. Phonetic transcriptions carry a stress mark (e.g. ['patu], [do'ku-dʒa-ʋi], [ba'hi], [ke'ti]) but no placement rule is stated.

sources.note: Sec. 2.4 'Accent' p.212: 'The Tucano languages have accent, or pitch accent systems in which there is high pitch vs low pitch.. High pitch is generally associated with accent. Some of the languages, such as Desano, Tuyuca, Yuruti and Cubeo, have one accented syllable per phonological word.' Family survey; Yurutí data credited to Kinch & Kinch 1992 ms 'El yurutí' (ICC atlas draft). No placement rule for Yurutí.

sources.note: Sec. 1.1 'El sistema tonal' p.45: all East Tucanoan varieties except Pisamira have two phonological pitch levels; Yurutí (YR) example dii 'sangre' vs díí 'carne'. Pisamira alone described as accentual. Nothing on accent placement in Yurutí.
